subject: QBR prep — launch slotting, delivery cadence, and contingency scan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep — launch slotting, delivery cadence, and contingency scan

Hi all — kicking off a short QBR prep thread to align on the product + eng picture for Acme’s pilot launch windows. Key asks below and a tentative timeline in the attached matrix (Attachment: QBR_launch_matrix.xlsx - spreadsheet).

Quick context: Acme wants a phased pilot across two customer cohorts (pilot A: late May; pilot B: early July). We need a clear view of delivery-relevant risks, ownership, and one-page contingency plans for any 2-week slip.

Please reply with:
- A concise status line per team (on-track / at-risk / blocked).
- Top 2 delivery risks you want the leadership team to own.
- A named owner and recommended contingency (rollback, reduced scope, capacity bump).

Proposed timeline:
- By EOD Fri 3/16: internal status + risk list.
- Tue 3/20 10:00–10:30 PT: 30-min aligned run-through (calendar invite forthcoming).

Attachments: QBR_launch_matrix.xlsx (driver matrix with slots & owners).

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: QBR_launch_matrix.xlsx)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — launch slotting, delivery cadence, and contingency scan

On Thu, Mar 15, 2028 at 9:12 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi all — kicking off a short QBR prep thread to align on the product + eng picture for Acme’s pilot launch windows...

Status (eng): at-risk.
Top delivery risks (top 2):
- Nervecore regression in 2.3 branch that increases tail latency under mixed workload (impact: pilot A latency targets).
- GPU slot contention in us-west-2 during the last pre-launch week (we currently share burst capacity with other Dedicated pools).

Named owners & proposed contingency:
- Nervecore regression -> owner: Marcus Lin. Contingency: roll forward a hotfix branch + apply targeted KV-cache bypass; if hotfix fails, we have a reduced-feature mode (disable streaming optimizations) that preserves correctness at ~1.4x latency.
- GPU slot contention -> owner: Monica Patel (ops). Contingency: short-term dedicated burst reservation for pilot A (cost add) or shift pilot A to an alternate slot 1 week later.

I attached a 2-page summary with perf traces and proposed timeline for the hotfix path.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime
(Attachment: eng_updates_20280315.pdf)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — launch slotting, delivery cadence, and contingency scan

Thanks for the quick update, Marcus and Priyom. A few directives before the Tues sync: 

1) Risk heatmap: Marcus, please convert your two risks into a one-page heatmap (likelihood x customer impact) and drop in the shared QBR folder by EOD Mon 3/19. Use the template in the Drive link.
2) Decision owners: assign a single decision owner per mitigation (this is critical — no dual-owners). Add brief decision criteria (e.g., if latency > 450ms p95 for 3 sequential runs -> trigger reduced-feature mode).
3) Cost escalation: Monica — prepare a cost estimate for the dedicated burst reservation option (delta for 2-week reservation). If cost > $10k, flag for exec approval and include a trade-off note (time vs. cost).
4) Customer communication: Lauren, draft a short MAP (mutual action plan) for Acme that we can share after the Tue alignment; include acceptance criteria for pilot A. Tara, we’ll share it in draft for your review before sending.

I’m copying Monica and Lauren so we can close the action items quickly. If any of these owners think the mitigation won't be ready by Tue, escalate to me now so we can triage scope.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Product & Ops, Redwood Inference

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Monica — cost delta estimate request

Monica — please pull the Dedicated burst pricing delta and include both hourly and 2-week flat estimates. Add any compliance/approval gating that would slow a rapid reservation.
From: Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — launch slotting, delivery cadence, and contingency scan

Thanks, Priyom and team — appreciate the early alignment. A few items from Acme's side: 

- We are comfortable with the proposed pilot slots (late May / early July) but would prefer an explicit contingency that keeps pilot A in calendar May rather than shifting into June. The MAP should include a defined acceptance gate and rollback signal.
- On the Nervecore regression: can you confirm whether reduced-feature mode will still allow the core ACME workflow (search + rerank) to function with degraded UX? We need that assurance for our execs.
- We will share our internal acceptance criteria doc (Attachment: acme_requirements.docx) and would like to get the draft MAP by 3/20 as requested.

One ask: please add a short line in the MAP that explains the rollback user experience (what customers will see if we enable reduced-feature mode). This helps with our internal comms.

DocuSign: we are prepared to sign the standard pilot MAP once we review the draft — linking here for reference: https://docusign.example/acme-map

Regards —
Tara Liu
Director, Cloud Integrations, Acme Cloud
(Attachment: acme_requirements.docx)
